title: Helix Finance - Dedicated capacity discovery
summary: Discovery focused on Helix Finance's need for dedicated GPU capacity with strict isolation, burst/burstback behavior, and predictable latency for low-latency trading alerts and compliance redaction. Security and residency requirements push them toward Redwood Dedicated with VPC options; they requested a benchmark and pricing for a reserved pool plus controlled burst to hosted capacity.
next_steps: Redwood to share Dedicated pricing and a sample committed capacity proposal (Janelle) by 2026-04-06
SE to run benchmark with Helix sample payloads and 2 workload profiles and share results by 2026-04-09
Send SOC2/ISO docs and KMS integration notes (Marcus) by 2026-04-05
Follow-up technical deep dive to be scheduled week of 2026-04-13
action_items: Janelle Park (AE): Send committed capacity proposal + pricing sheet by 2026-04-06
Marcus Li (SE): Run perf benchmark with Helix dataset (low-latency alerting and batch embed) and deliver results by 2026-04-09
Daniela Ruiz: Share Redwood Dedicated architecture diagram and burst policy examples by 2026-04-05
Sofia Kim (Helix): Provide sample PII redaction policy and compliance contacts by 2026-04-06
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-02 15:00 UTC | Duration 52m | Attendees: Janelle Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Daniela Ruiz (Redwood SE), Ravi Shah (CTO - Helix), Lena Ortiz (Head of ML), Owen Park (Infra Lead), Sofia Kim (Security)

[00:00] Janelle: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros — I'm Janelle, AE on the account, Marcus is our SE who will do the deep dive. Can you do quick intros on your side?
[00:12] Ravi: Yeah hi, I'm Ravi, CTO at Helix. We're exploring options for running our inference workload more predictably, so thanks for the time.
[00:20] Lena: Lena here, heads up ML. We're currently using hosted endpoints for prototyping but need something more consistent for production.
[00:29] Owen: Owen, infra. We care about VPC isolation, key management, and burst behaviour — we can't have noisy neighbors.
[00:36] Sofia: Sofia, security. We'll want SOC 2 + KMS + SSO details.
[00:41] Marcus: Great, thanks. Today we'll focus on dedicated capacity — reserved GPUs — and how we handle burst to hosted, autoscaling policies, and security. We'll also capture requirements for a bench.

[02:05] Marcus: Can you describe your current traffic patterns? qps, latencies, sequences?
[02:12] Lena: Sure. We have two main workloads: 1) real-time trading alerts, very latency sensitive, small prompts, 30-100 tokens, spikes to 250 qps during market events; 2) nightly batch embedding and rerank jobs for reconciliation, large sequences up to 1k tokens but throughput-oriented. Right now hosted endpoints struggle at those spikes cost-effectively.

[04:00] Owen: Important note: data residency — customer data must stay in our VPC and we need audit logs for all model calls. We're evaluating Dedicated with Private control plane.
[04:12] Janelle: Understood. Our Dedicated offering supports a private VPC peering option or on-prem bundle for strict residency. We provide per-request audit logs and can integrate with your KMS.

[06:45] Lena: For the trading alerts we need p95 latency < 150ms for generation at peak. Is that achievable with reserved GPUs?
[06:54] Marcus: Yes, for small prompts on a pinned model variant on a dedicated GPU pool we can meet that latency. It depends on model choice and batching settings. We'll need to run a benchmark with your exact prompts. The other factor is how you want to handle bursts. Do you want guaranteed capacity for peaks or graceful fallbacks?

[08:30] Ravi: Ideally guaranteed for the critical path (alerts). For non-critical batch we can use lower priority capacity or hosted fallbacks. Cost is a big factor — dedicated pools with 24/7 reserved hardware are heavier commitment.
[09:05] Daniela: Redwood Dedicated supports reserved pools and a configurable burst policy. You can reserve N GPU slots for guaranteed throughput and allow controlled burst to our hosted pool when reserved capacity is saturated. There's also autoscaling within the dedicated pool but it's subject to commit limits.

[10:22] Owen: How does the burst to hosted work security-wise? Can we ensure the payload doesn't leave our control or is redacted?
[10:31] Marcus: Good question. If you choose the VPC private option, network egress can be controlled; however bursting to our hosted multi-tenant pool means requests will hit Redwood-hosted infra. For sensitive workloads you can configure selective routing: critical endpoints always served from Dedicated, non-sensitive endpoints allowed to burst. We also support edge-level masking and pre-call redaction before potential host bursting.

[12:50] Sofia: And encryption — we require customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for model inputs at rest.
[12:57] Marcus: We support KMS integrations and can encrypt model cache and logs with customer-managed keys. We'll share our KMS integration guide.

[15:10] Lena: For scaling, during market spikes we saw 10x baseline qps for 20-30 minutes. If we reserve for baseline and allow burst, what's the observed degradation when bursting?
[15:24] Marcus: When bursting, you'd see higher tail latencies as requests are routed to hosted variants or queued; Redwood's smart routing tries region/variant fallbacks to meet latency SLOs but there's a cost/latency tradeoff. We can set hard caps where after X% saturation we return best-effort results or degrade model complexity. We can also use prefix/KV cache to reduce duplicate work for repeated contexts.

[17:40] Ravi: Pricing — what's the cost model for reserved GPUs + burst?
[17:47] Janelle: Reserved is monthly commit for GPU hours; burst is billed at hosted on-demand rates and you only pay for what you use. We'll put together a simple projection based on your baseline + expected burst minutes. That'll be in the committed capacity proposal.

[19:30] Owen: On infra — how do you handle autoscaling in the dedicated pool? Do we get control for scale up/down thresholds?
[19:40] Daniela: Yes, autoscale policies are configurable. Policies can be target-latency, queue-depth, or scheduled. You can set min/max GPU counts. We also offer burst credits for short spikes to avoid immediate scaling events which are slower.

[21:05] Lena: We need an idea of throughput per GPU for the models we use — we're looking at 7B/13B variants.
[21:14] Marcus: We'll run throughput numbers in the bench. Typically a quantized 13B on A100-like hardware with optimized kernels gives X tokens/sec depending on prompt length. We'll provide a model performance profile for your workload.

[23:50] Sofia: Audit logs — we need immutable logs for every request with request IDs and user mapping for compliance.
[24:00] Marcus: Redwood provides request-level audit logs, TTL configurable, and export to your SIEM via syslog or S3. We can also redact PII at the ingestion layer if you prefer.

[26:10] Ravi: What about model version pinning and rollouts? We can't risk a silent model change affecting production.
[26:18] Daniela: You can pin model versions per route and control rollouts with canary policies; Redwood supports A/B and automatic rollback on quality regressions tied to your evals.

[28:45] Owen: Network architecture — do you support private control plane in our account?
[28:52] Marcus: Yes, Dedicated can be deployed with a private control plane in your VPC. There's a private peering option or a self-hosted control plane package if you need air-gapped. We'll share the architecture diagrams.

[31:10] Lena: Okay, so immediate asks: 1) bench with our prompts and sequences, 2) committed capacity pricing, 3) security docs including SOC2/KMS and private control plane specifics.
[31:21] Janelle: Yep we'll do that. Marcus, Daniela will take the bench and docs.

[33:05] Marcus: A couple of notes on benching: we'll need a sample of production prompt traffic and sequences, target concurrency, and any routing rules you expect. Also, if you want exact p95 numbers, we'll run both dedicated-only and dedicated+burst to measure tail behavior.
[33:25] Lena: We'll provide 24 hours of anonymized sample traffic and a list of example prompts. Owen and Sofia will sign off on data sharing.

[35:50] Ravi: Any references or peers who have used this? We're evaluating Lambda Labs and Paperspace too.
[35:57] Janelle: Many fintech customers use Redwood Dedicated for isolation and predictable economics. We'll share customer references and a case study.

[38:10] Owen: If we commit to N GPUs, what's the SLA?
[38:16] Daniela: Dedicated comes with an SLA on uptime and baseline latency SLOs for reserved pools; the specific numbers are in the enterprise agreement and vary by commit. We'll include the SLI targets in the proposal.

[40:40] Sofia: Security question — SSO and RBAC?
[40:45] Marcus: We support SAML SSO, fine-grained RBAC, and audit trails. Roles can be scoped per-route or per-project.

[43:30] Janelle: Quick recap: Redwood will deliver a committed capacity proposal and pricing, SE team will run the benchmark with Helix sample traffic, share SOC2/KMS/private control plane docs, and schedule a follow-up deep dive. Anything to add?
[43:48] Lena: Timeline looks good. We want bench results before next leadership review on 2026-04-15.

[45:10] Owen: One more operational question — how do you handle model fallback if the pinned variant isn't available?
[45:17] Marcus: There are automated fallback policies: fall back to a compatible quantized variant or route to hosted equivalents. You can set fallback behavior to strict (fail) or permissive (fallback).

[47:30] Ravi: Great. For the bench, can you also test prefix/KV cache effectiveness? We see a lot of repeated contexts in alerts.
[47:37] Marcus: Yes we'll include prefix cache scenarios and measure token savings and latency improvements.

[49:05] Daniela: We'll also include a runbook for burst tuning and recommended autoscale thresholds based on the bench.

[50:20] Janelle: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and schedule the deep dive.
[50:28] Ravi: Thanks all, appreciate it.

End of transcript.
